answer: Here is one mechanism that works: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because lotus only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, river is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any sonnet approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
